findings.desc: quality-cleanup: authority-signing.ts:102-107 — try-catch around Buffer.from(input, "base64") is dead code. Node.js Buffer.from(str, "base64") never throws on malformed base64; it silently ignores invalid characters and returns a buffer of whatever it decoded. The catch block at lines 105-107 is unreachable. The only guard that actually fires is the buf.length !== expectedLen check at line 108, which emits the generic "expected 32 raw bytes, got N" message instead of the never-reachable "invalid base64 (...)" message. Misleading diagnostic: callers cannot see the intended invalid-base64 error. Fix: remove the try-catch wrapper around Buffer.from (it is dead), rely solely on the length check, and optionally add a comment explaining that Buffer.from silently ignores invalid base64 chars.
